physical.notes: The cabinet/coin door wiring diagram (PDF page 125) draws the Memory Protect Switch, N.O., from CPU board CN6 pin 12 (BLK-RED) to the BLK ground. se.c's ram_w refuses writes to the protected RAM while public -3 is 1, and sega.vbs names the address swMemoryProtect; a closed coin door is public -3 at 1 and an open door 0. The Diagnostic Aids page: 'Opening the Coin Door will initiate a Factory Restore (Reset), by opening the Memory Protect Switch.'

Printed dedicated switch DS-6 (#6 VOLUME (RED BUTTON) (In Test: LEFT)), wired GRY-BLU to CN6-P8 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The cabinet wiring diagram draws it among the PORTALS™ SERVICE BUTTONS on the coin door; the harness runs drove the ROM's service menus with it.

Printed dedicated switch DS-7 (#7 SERV. CRED. (GREEN BUTTON) (In Test: RIGHT)), wired GRY-VIO to CN6-P9 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The cabinet wiring diagram draws it among the PORTALS™ SERVICE BUTTONS on the coin door; the harness runs drove the ROM's service menus with it.

Printed dedicated switch DS-8 (#8 BEGIN TEST (BLACK BUTTON) (In Test: ENTER)), wired GRY-BLK to CN6-P10 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The cabinet wiring diagram draws it among the PORTALS™ SERVICE BUTTONS on the coin door; the harness runs drove the ROM's service menus with it.

Printed switch-matrix drive column 1, return row 1. The grid prints "LT BUTTON (UK ONLY)" with the location "Cabinet Side" and the part cell "180-5160-00". The 5.00 ROM's Switch Test names it "LT BUTTON (UK ONLY) / GRN-BRN WHT-BRN #01". UK only: the grid prints the name on a grey panel, and the cabinet wiring diagram's boxed note reads 'UK ONLY: 2 Extra Cabinet Buttons for the Post Save™ Feature are used. The Left Button operates the Left Outlane Ball Deflector. The Right Button operates the Right Outlane Ball Deflector. Both buttons pushed together operate the Center Up/Down Post. Both buttons are located under the Flipper Buttons.' Its UK drawing puts the LEFT BUTTON, N.O., on WHT-BRN (CN7 pin 9) and GRN-BRN (CN5 pin 1). PinMAME publishes none of the UK post-save coils (see the auxiliary outputs), so a recreation has no deflector to drive from this button.

mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest in the 4-Ball Trough on micro switches 11 (left), 12 and 13 (Roller Actuator, Lite-Force, 180-5119-02) and on the up-kicker opto 14; the Dual OPTO boards carry 14 on the lower beam (LED1) and the stacking opto 15 on the upper beam (LED2), which only a double-stacked ball breaks. Q1 (26-1200) kicks the ball on 14 up past 15 into the shooter lane, and the rest roll one place toward the up-kicker. Hold each occupied position at 1 and pass the kicked ball through 15 as a short 1 pulse (beam blocked). In the gameplay run the ROM fired Q1 about 1.1 s after Start and repeated it about every 1.25 s until the scenario moved the served ball to 16; in the stacking-opto run a rise of 15 drew six Q1 kicks and then the auto launch Q2, the ROM's jam clearing. The retained table pulses 15 from its Q1 callback.

mechanisms.behavior: A served ball comes to rest on the shooter-lane switch 16 and leaves past the shooter lane exit switch 10. The Ball Shooter (Plunger) Autoplunger Arm assembly carries the auto-launch coil Q2 (23-800); the cabinet also has a manual plunger, which the retained table models beside its impulse plunger. In the gameplay run the ROM did not fire Q2 while the ball rested on 16 for 6 s, and fired it 0.17 s after the right flipper button was pressed while no ball was on 16 and in ball search; the Diagnostic Aids page names '#16 Shooter Lane & #2 Auto Launch' as a pair the CPU retries about ten times before reporting the switch.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: The Elvis assembly (reference 500-6796-00) carries the molded figure (torso, legs and two arms) on a platform riveted assembly over a welded carrier frame; a Haydon 46868-12-002 12 V DC stepper motor (Stepper Motor Assembly 500-6809-00) turns a 7.25" threaded shaft that moves it. The ELVIS test page describes one full RUN cycle as back-to-front or front-to-back, and the home switch 33 (Micro Switch (Short Actuator, Bend) 180-5189-00) as closed with Elvis 'in the Home Position or closest to the Upper Playfield'. The stepper's four phases are Q25-Q28; elvis.c counts the order 0x0c, 0x06, 0x03, 0x09 as one direction and the reverse as the other. Two Coil (29-1400) & Conn. assemblies (500-6818-00 and -01) pull the actuator wires for the legs (Q29) and the arms (Q30); IPDB describes the toy's shaking hips and gesturing hands, which bring the microphone to his lips. The four KING stand-up targets 36-39 (515-7381-00) sit on the figure's base and travel with it. The ELVIS test: RUN runs the stepper one full cycle, PULSE pulses it, LEGS and ARMS energize Q29 and Q30, and on power-up the mechanism returns to its HOME position. In the ELVIS-test harness run, RUN drove the phases and left 33 open, a second RUN closed it, PULSE moved the figure off home, and LEGS and ARMS drove Q29 and Q30; every run drove the phases at boot and left 33 closed. In a game the ROM ran the phases with the legs and arms from many scoring switches. The retained table moves the stand primitive with a one-solenoid cvpmMech on Q25 alone (150 steps, 33 at step 0), a stand-in that ignores Q26-Q28 and the direction.
mechanisms.label: Dancing Elvis figure

positions.description: Figure at the end of its travel closest to the upper playfield; the position after power-up.
positions.label: Home

mechanisms.behavior: The 5-Bank Drop Target assembly: five white drop targets (545-6102-01) on drop-target switches 17-21 (180-5158-00, diodes on the terminal strip), spelling E-L-V-I-S, and the 24-940 reset coil Q3. A down target holds its switch closed. In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed Q3 0.33 s after the fifth target went down and twice more 0.41 s apart; it also reset the bank at boot and at Start.
mechanisms.label: ELVIS 5-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: The Hotel Door Coil, Frame, Stand-Up assembly: a 27-1500 coil (Q19) with the Plunger Assembly 515-7409-00 and Actuator Arm 535-9478-00 moves the Metal Door (Hotel) 535-9477-00. The door's micro switch 63 (180-5119-02) and the two 1" stand-up targets 52 (top) and 53 (bottom) on the mini-playfield behind it complete it. The ROM holds Q19 on for long stretches: in the gameplay run it switched Q19 on when 52 closed and while a ball rested in either saucer or on the hotel post, and in the hound-dog probe 0.13 s after 63 rose and about 65 ms after each hound-dog hit. The retained table drops doorwall and swings the flipper-shaped door fDoor open while Q19 is on.
mechanisms.label: Heartbreak Hotel door

mechanisms.behavior: A ball held at the hotel post rests on micro switch 48 (180-5189-00); the hotel lock release Q7 (23-800, with the Solid Plunger Assembly (Short) 515-6119-02 on the Magnet Coil, Bracket and Ball Lock page) releases it. In the gameplay run a ball held on 48 for 6 s drew no Q7; Q7 fired only in ball search. The retained table holds the ball in the kicker HLock and kicks it on Q7.
mechanisms.label: Hotel ball lock

mechanisms.behavior: The Ball Eject (Left) assembly, drawing labelled SW. 34: a ball resting on micro switch 34 (180-5186-00) is kicked out by Q6 (24-940). In the gameplay run the ROM kicked about 4.3 s after the ball arrived and twice more about 0.7 s apart while it stayed.
mechanisms.label: Center saucer (Ball Eject Left)

mechanisms.behavior: The Ball Eject (Right) assembly, drawing labelled SW. 32: a ball resting on micro switch 32 (180-5186-00) is kicked out by Q12 (24-940, TOP EJECT). In the gameplay run the ROM kicked once about 5.7 s after the ball arrived.
mechanisms.label: Top saucer (Ball Eject Right)

mechanisms.behavior: A 22-650 magnet coil (500-6808-00, diode in its connector) under the playfield on Q5; it has no switch of its own. In the gameplay run it fired only in ball search. The retained table models it as a cvpmMagnet around the trigger Magnet that grabs balls while Q5 is on.
mechanisms.label: Magnet

mechanisms.behavior: A mini-coil assembly (515-6543-00, coil 32-1800) on Q8; the manual names no switch for it. Only the ROM's Single Coil Test fired it in the harness runs. The retained table holds the gate CGate open while Q8 is on.
mechanisms.label: Control gate

mechanisms.behavior: The Hound Dog Pop-Up Target (assembly reference 500-6781-00): the dog figure 500-6820-00 on a base bracket with an actuator bracket, a deflector pad and the micro switch 64 (180-5190-28); it has no coil. The ROM reads 64 as hit at public 0, so the contact rests closed and a hit opens it. In the hound-dog probe each hit made the ROM switch the hotel door Q19 on about 65 ms later. The retained table animates the dog primitive and pulses 64 to 1, the opposite level.
mechanisms.label: Hound dog pop-up target

mechanisms.behavior: Left and right lower flipper assemblies with 22-900 (YELLOW) coils and E.O.S. switches 180-5149-00, on one 50v supply. The CPU applies a 40 ms pulse on a button closure and then 1 ms every 12 ms while the button is held; each N.C. end-of-stroke switch opens at full stroke, and a closure during a hold earns another 40 ms pulse. PinMAME publishes Q15 at 47/48 and Q16 at 45/46 and writes the E.O.S. inputs 81 and 83 itself.
mechanisms.label: Lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Upper left and upper right flipper assemblies with 23-900 (GREEN) coils, red bat bushings and spacers in place of an E.O.S. switch. The left cabinet button (84) works both left flippers; the right cabinet button is double-stacked, a half press (82) working the lower right flipper and a full press (82 and 88) both right flippers. In the gameplay run 84 drove Q13 with the lower left flipper, 88 drove Q14, and 82 alone never drove Q14. The retained table rotates its upper flippers from the lower-flipper callbacks.
mechanisms.label: Upper flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q9/49), right (Q10/50) and bottom (Q11/51) pop bumpers with 26-1200 coils, stack switches 180-5015-05 mounted in reverse and #555 G.I. bulbs under the caps; each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay run.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q17/59) and right (Q18/62) slingshots with 23-800 coils, two blade contacts per side, only one of them with a diode; each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay run.
mechanisms.label: Slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: UK only: the coil chart's auxiliary group drives a left up/down post (AUX 1, 26-1200), a centre up/down post (AUX 2, 23-1100) and a right up/down post (AUX 3, 26-1200) from the UK 3X Transistor Driver Board 520-5068-01; the cabinet wiring diagram calls the outer two the outlane ball deflectors, and the parts pages show a UK Up/Down Post and a UK Ball Deflector. The UK cabinet buttons 1 (left deflector) and 8 (right deflector), pressed together for the centre post, ask the ROM for them, and standard adjustment 39 enables the feature (UK default YES). elvisGameData declares no auxiliary board, so PinMAME publishes none of the three outputs; the mechanism has no actuator a recreation can bind.
mechanisms.label: UK post save (unpublished)

se.c sets public 15 while the ROM's fast-flip byte is non-zero, i.e. while the flippers are enabled in a game; MACHINE_INIT(se3) places that byte at CPU RAM 0x04 for every se3 game, so all twenty-one Elvis sets publish it. sega.vbs declares GameOnSolenoid = 15. In the gameplay and hound-dog runs it rose at Start. Physical Q15 is the left flipper at public 48; never wire this state to a transistor.
se_solenoid_w masks physical Q16 off public 16 and publishes it at 45/46; nothing else drives 16.

physical.location: Elvis figure stepper motor under the playfield
physical.notes: Coils Detailed Chart Table (DR. 6) row #25 "STEPPER #1": drive transistor Q25, control RED J6-P1, cell "Stepper Motor Only / 041-5069-00". The 5.00 ROM's Single Coil Test names it "#25 STEPPER #1 / GRY-RED RED" (power wire, then control wire). The type cell is merged across rows #25-#28 and printed once. The driver board diagram draws 'STEPPER MOTOR 041-5069-00 Haydon Nº 46868-12-002' as two centre-tapped windings, its RED, GRN, BLK and BLU leads on J6-1 to J6-4 and both centre taps on a lug under the playfield fed 'FROM GRY-RED Power Out +12v DC J16-P3'. Retained table script: the cvpmMech mElvis moves the figure while 25 is on (Sol1 = 25, lines 147-154), and UpdateElvis moves the stand primitive pStand (lines 190-196). In the harness runs the ROM drove the four phases at boot, while the figure danced in play, and on RUN and PULSE in the ELVIS test. Placement from the retained table's Primitive pStand (projection: the cvpmMech mElvis (Sol1 = 25, AddSw 33) models the figure's travel with no switch, motor or coil object; projected onto the figure's stand primitive pStand, which UpdateElvis moves).

physical.notes: One G.I. relay on the I/O Power Driver Board 520-5137-01 (U206 74HCT273 data latch output 1Q from D0 through R254 1K to the Q200 2N3904 relay driver, coil on 20v DC with D229 1N4004 across it) switches the 5.7v AC G.I. supply from J14 (YEL pins 1-3, YEL-WHT pins 4-6) through four 5A slow-blow fuses to the four circuits on J15 (General Illumination Circuit Detailed Wiring Diagram, PDF page 120): B, F24, BRN-WHT to WHT-BRN, 'Back Panel X10; Pops X3 Upper Right Corner X1', 11 #44 and 3 #555; Y, F25, YELLOW to WHT-YEL, 'Mid Left & Lower Playfield X15', 15 #44 and 1 #555; G, F26, GREEN to WHT-GRN, 'Upper Playfield X10 + US Coin Door X2 (Euro X3)', 10 #44 then 2 #555 on the coin door; V, F27, VIOLET to WHT-VIO, 'Mid Right Playfield X6', 5 #44 and 1 #555 (its last socket printed #5*). The quantity 48 is those printed counts with the US coin door's two; the page warns '* G.I. Bulb quantities may change during production.' The pop bumper bulbs are G.I. (the Bumper page lists a #555 under each cap), and the back panel's ten 'GIs on rear Back Panel' are circuit B. se.c publishes the relay as GI 0 (on while its latch bit is low). The harness runs saw it on in attract mode, off from Start until the served ball reached the shooter lane, and blinking with the TC(B) target 24, the KIN(G) target 39, the scarf standup 40 and a ball arriving in either saucer or on the hotel post. The retained table declares UseGI = 0 (line 40) and sets GICallback = GetRef("GIUpdate") (line 1038), whose sub switches the aGiLights and aGiFlashers collections. The placements are the 6 members of aGiLights that draw their bulb mesh (gi10, gi11, gi13, gi14, gi27, gi9), observed only; the drawing's circuit discs have not been matched to them, so no placement carries a string. The other 26 members (gi1, gi12, gi15, gi16, gi17, gi18, gi19, gi2, gi20, gi21, gi22, gi23, gi24, gi25, gi26, gi28, gi29, gi3, gi30, gi31, gi32, gi4, gi5, gi6, gi7, gi8) are bulb-mode Lights that show no bulb mesh, with no primitive modelling a socket under them, so they sit on no bulb and make no socket. The rest of the 48, including the back panel's ten and the coin door's two, are counted but not placed.
